# Rings Network

> Rings is a decentralized, browser-native structured peer-to-peer (P2P) and Sphinx onion network. Browser tabs and native daemons join one Chord DHT overlay, address each other by DID, exchange messages over direct WebRTC datachannels with zero central data servers, and route TCP, UDP, HTTPS, and composable Kleisli `invoke` traffic through multi-hop Sphinx/AEZ onion circuits—serving as an embeddable, browser-native alternative to Tor, I2P, and server-relayed overlays. Rust workspace, AGPL-3.0-only (commercial licensing available), https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings.

This file follows https://llmstxt.org/. It is for agents that evaluate Rings, build on it, or change it: which document is authoritative for what, how the crates are layered, how each target is built and tested, and which conventions a change must keep. Where this file and the code disagree, the code wins; correct this file in the same change.

## What Rings is

- Overlay (communication layer): a Chord DHT (`K = 4` successor list, 160-bit finger table, non-transitive multi-predecessor and 1-hop gap-bridge hints, voluntary `Leave` handoffs) keyed by DID with `network_id` overlay isolation. It provides authenticated O(log N) routing, actor-isolated Merkle-authenticated CRDT data topics (`co_dots`, per-`(digest, author)` tombstones, `co_registers`, zero-tombstone `LeaseHeartbeat`), chain-replicated relay-inbox storage, and end-to-end ElGamal stream encryption after a peer handshake.
- Privacy layer: guard-closed Sphinx/AEZ v5 onion loops in `crates/node/src/onion`, fixed-width cells over direct edges through pinned entry guards, dormant-by-default outbound lanes (`OnionIdleFloor::OFF`, zero idle cover traffic) with active-window constant-rate slot pacing substituting real cells for cover (and configurable background cover floor), paid `SlotRoster` admission, fixed cell size classes, SURB reply blocks, world-facing `tcp`/`https`/`udp` exits, and 120 typed `invoke<In, Out, L>` Kleisli pipeline shapes (`Σ = {relay} ⊎ Σ_I ⊎ Σ_W`, including `turn.ticket`). Each relay learns only its immediate predecessor and successor, while exits process payloads without learning client identity. The layer contracts are defined in SECURITY.md under Layer Contracts.
- Transport: decoupled `TransportInterface` and `ConnectionInterface` (`crates/transport`, configurable via `network: { kind, params }`), supporting 0–8 step binary `HandshakeStep` negotiation, WebRTC datachannels (`native-webrtc`, `web-sys-webrtc`), quiet-window ICE candidate settling, bounded static-dictionary LZ4 wire compression for `DhtControl`/`Storage` frames and compact `WirePayload` encoding (`WIRE_VERSION = 6`, `480 B` max chunk envelope overhead down from `742 B`), and stateless signature+ECDH TURN relay (`rings-turn` over UDP and TCP `?transport=tcp` with round-robin single-TURN selection) plus DHT-discovered Onion TURN (`rings-turn-service` over split-trust multi-hop `onion::udp`) for Symmetric NAT and UDP-blocked firewall traversal. Data flows directly peer to peer; seed nodes assist initial bootstrap discovery.
- Identity: a DID derived from a public key. Signature schemes: secp256k1 (EIP-191, bip137), secp256r1 (P-256), ed25519, BLS; the browser console signs with WebCrypto P-256, MetaMask, or Phantom. DIDs pair short-lived session delegations with slot-isolated admission, with epoch-randomized ring placement (#780) and DRanking trust algebra (#748) on the 2.0 track. SECURITY.md is authoritative for security architecture claims.
- Protocol runtime: `Protocol::step` is pure (state, event -> state, effects); an `Interpret` shell performs the effects through a namespace-scoped capability. Built-in protocols: relay (TCP/UDP tunnels over the overlay), echo, DID mail, and TURN ticket issuance. Applications register their own by namespace: `provider.register_protocol(..)` in Rust, `provider.on(namespace, initialState, handler)` in JavaScript.
- Targets: the native daemon (`rings` CLI with JSON-RPC API over HTTP), the interactive terminal dashboard (`rings-tui`), standalone and overlay TURN servers (`rings-turn`, `rings-turn-service`), authoritative DNS relay (`rings-dns-relay`), mail gateway (`rings-mail-gateway`), selective IPv4/TCP TUN gateway (`rings-gateway` + `gateway-config-unix`), the browser/Wasm node (npm `@ringsnetwork/rings-node`; the rings.rs frontend and Chrome MV3 extension with Onion WebView), and a C FFI (`crates/node/include/rings.h`).

## Status

- Shipped in 1.0: the Chord overlay with range-proved finger convergence, non-transitive gap bridging, and voluntary `Leave`, native and browser nodes, wire-versioned framing (`WIRE_VERSION = 6`) with bounded LZ4 compression, decoupled `TransportInterface` and multi-step `HandshakeStep`, the onion privacy layer with client-sealed Sphinx/AEZ Kleisli pipelines (#834, `tcp`/`https`/`udp` exits, `invoke` backends such as `turn.ticket`, TUN gateway, onion WebView), `rings-turn` (UDP/TCP) + `rings-turn-service` (DHT discovery + multi-hop `onion::udp`), `rings-tui`, group-committed replay protection, slot-isolated resource accounting, per-origin rate quotas, clock-bounded authenticated CRDT removal stability, chain-replicated relay custody, DRanking provisional service-receipt evidence collection, a public seed (https://node.rings.rs), and the hosted console (https://rings.rs/#node).
- Roadmap: adaptive churn telemetry and tuning (#773-#779), followed by 2.0 epoch-randomized ring positions (#780) and DRanking decentralized trust ranking (#748). See ROADMAP.md.
- To evaluate Rings, read README.md, SECURITY.md, and ROADMAP.md, in that order.

## Documentation

- [Documentation book](https://rings.rs/docs/): the reference, including the comparison of Rings with Tor, I2P, Nym, libp2p, Nostr, and WebTorrent; source in `docs/src`, built with mdBook and published from master.
- [Engineering Blog](https://rings.rs/blog/): deep-dive essays on decentralized TURN over onion circuits, Onion OP, Chord finger-table convergence, and algebraic correctness (`examples/frontend/article/`, Atom feed at `https://rings.rs/blog/feed.xml`).
- [Guide](https://rings.rs/#guide): the abridged version: one card per runtime and the first commands; the book is authoritative.
- [README](https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings/blob/master/README.md): overview, architecture table, examples, whitepaper citation.
- [UPGRADING.md](https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings/blob/master/UPGRADING.md): 1.0 frozen contracts (`WIRE_VERSION = 6`, delegation verification, C FFI ABI, control API) and operator upgrade checklist.
- [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings/blob/master/SECURITY.md): security architecture, layer contracts, feature guarantees, deployment models, and vulnerability reporting.
- [ROADMAP.md](https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings/blob/master/ROADMAP.md): shipped foundations and the network-layer and privacy-layer tracks.
- [Whitepaper & Protocol Papers](https://rings.rs/papers/): dedicated web full-text and PDF reading hub for the unified [Rings 1.0 Whitepaper](https://rings.rs/papers/rings/) (`https://rings.rs/papers/rings.pdf`, `papers/rings.tex`) and the [DRanking 2.0 Specification](https://rings.rs/papers/dranking/) (`https://rings.rs/papers/dranking.pdf`, `papers/dranking.tex`).
- [JSON-RPC API](https://rings.rs/docs/jsonrpc.html): every method of the node API (plus provider-local RPC extensions) with curl examples.
- [config.yaml](https://rings.rs/docs/advanced-topic/config.yaml.html): the complete generated node configuration, section by section.
- [Operate a Node from the CLI](https://rings.rs/docs/cli.html): every `rings` subcommand and delegation rotation mode.
- [Interactive Terminal UI (TUI)](https://rings.rs/docs/tui.html): 6-tab Ratatui workbench (`rings-tui`) for live monitoring and commands.
- [Onion Routing & Kleisli Pipelines](https://rings.rs/docs/onion.html): Sphinx/AEZ loops, `tcp`/`https`/`udp` exits, and composable `invoke` operations.
- [Transport Abstraction](https://rings.rs/docs/advanced-topic/transport.html) and [Wire Protocol & LZ4 Compression](https://rings.rs/docs/advanced-topic/wire-protocol.html): decoupled traits, N-step handshakes, and frame encoding.
- [Operator Observability](https://rings.rs/docs/operator-observability.html): bounded telemetry via `GET /status?view=observability`.
- [Native Gateway](https://rings.rs/docs/native-gateway.html): selective IPv4/TCP TUN routing over onion loops and the `gateway-config-unix` helper.
- [DNS Relay](https://rings.rs/docs/dns-relay.html): authoritative `<did>.<zone>` DNS and IPv6 TCP ingress relay (`rings-dns-relay`).
- [TURN Server](https://rings.rs/docs/turn-server.html): stateless signature+ECDH RFC 5766 TURN over UDP/TCP (`rings-turn`) and DHT/Onion TURN (`rings-turn-service`).
- [Mail Gateway](https://rings.rs/docs/mail-gateway.html): zero-custody `did@domain` SMTP receiver and encrypted DHT mailbox polling (`rings-mail-gateway`).
- [Embed via C FFI](https://rings.rs/docs/ffi.html): the C ABI, its lifecycle and ownership rules, and the Python, Swift, and Kotlin wrappers.
- [Browser Node and Extension](https://rings.rs/docs/browser-node.html): the hosted console, running the frontend locally, and packaging the extension.

## Source map

- `crates/core`: Chord DHT, swarm, DID and elliptic-curve identity, message types, wire compression, DHT storage bounds. Protocol only: application registries and descriptors live in `node`.
- `crates/transport`: decoupled `TransportInterface` and `ConnectionInterface`, WebRTC transports (`native-webrtc`, `web-sys-webrtc`), TURN-over-TCP/TURNS client bridge, ICE candidate tier settling, and the `dummy` transport that topology tests run on.
- `crates/runtime`: runtime contracts (`sleep`, `Spawner`, `TaskSet`, `run_blocking`, `MaybeSend`) shared across native Tokio and the browser JavaScript event loop, sitting below `rings-transport`.
- `crates/node`: the node. Native daemon and CLI (`bin/rings.rs`, `src/native`), browser provider (`src/provider/browser`), FFI provider (`src/provider/ffi.rs`, feature `ffi`), extension runtime and built-in protocols (`src/extension`), mail gateway and recipient (`src/mail`), the privacy layer: onion loops, dormant-by-default active-window slot pacing, paid admission, exit/invoke registries, `onion::udp` (`src/onion`), JSON-RPC handlers (`src/rpc_impl.rs`), seeds, peer quotas, registries.
- `crates/rpc`: RPC types and the JSON-RPC client. Its protos are plain data mirrors of node types.
- `crates/codec`: the postcard/serde wire codec. `crates/derive`: proc macros, including `wasm_export`. `crates/aez`: AEZ v5 wide-block tweakable enciphering and authenticated encryption used by Sphinx onion body carry (`native` and `wasm32`).
- `crates/measure`: pure local peer credit, reliability, and DRanking provisional service-receipt evidence algorithms. `crates/network-policy`: the public-network admission policy for egress targets. `crates/dns-relay`: authoritative `<did>.<zone>` DNS and IPv6 TCP ingress relay. `crates/gateway`: the native TUN gateway that carries selected TCP destinations over onion loops (vendored netlink under `vendor/`). `crates/webview`: onion-backed WebView gateway primitives. `crates/turn`: the stateless RFC 5766 TURN server (`rings-turn`) over UDP and TCP (`?transport=tcp`) for Symmetric NAT / CGNAT and UDP-blocked firewall traversal using `DelegateeKey`, `Did`, or `Account` signatures paired with secp256k1 ECDH-derived credentials. `crates/turn-service`: composes `rings-turn` + `rings-node` for `turn_services` DHT discovery, `turn.ticket` Sphinx invoke, and opt-in multi-hop `onion::udp` relaying (`rings-turn-service`). `crates/tui`: the interactive terminal UI (`rings-tui`) for node monitoring, status inspection, and button command execution. `crates/logo`: dependency-free mathematical geometry and OKLCH color solver that deterministically generates all canonical Rings SVG and JSON logo assets. `crates/test-support`: shared deterministic test utilities.
- `examples/`: `frontend` (the Yew/Wasm web app, `article/` engineering articles rendered into `<site>/blog/` by `examples/frontend/scripts/build_article.py`, and Chrome MV3 extension, in its own Cargo workspace with TypeScript glue in `extension-assets/` and `scripts/`), `mailbox` (SMTP in, IMAP out, through a DNS relay or a mail gateway, and the mail gateway `rings-mail-gateway`), `native` and `relay` (workspace members), `dweb` (its own Yew workspace), `ffi` (Python, Swift, Kotlin wrappers and tests).
- `docs/`: the mdBook (`book.toml`, `src/`, `theme/`). `papers/`: the whitepaper and formal companion papers, compiled into `<site>/papers/` by `examples/frontend/scripts/build_papers.py` with first-party cookie-free telemetry in `workers/paper-telemetry/`.

## Build and test

- Toolchain: `rust-toolchain.toml` pins the stable compiler (`cargo +<pin> install --locked rings-node`); a pin bump updates README.md, `crates/node/README.md`, `docs/src/install-a-native-node.md`, and `examples/frontend/src/guide.rs`; formatting uses the pinned nightly rustfmt (`cargo +nightly-2026-07-02 fmt --all -- --check`). TOML is formatted with taplo; spelling is checked with typos.
- Native: `cargo build`; `cargo test --profile ci --all --all-targets` (or `--release`; `--profile ci` preserves release overflow/assertion semantics and optimizes dependencies, `rings-core`, and `rings-aez` at `opt-level = 3` without full LTO, see `.github/CI.md`); install the CLI with `cargo install --path crates/node`, then `rings init` and `rings run`.
- Wasm: `cargo clippy -p rings-node --features browser --no-default-features --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; the npm package is built by `wasm-pack build crates/node --release --scope ringsnetwork -t web --no-default-features --features browser_default` (`npm run wasm_pack`); browser tests use wasm-bindgen-test in headless Chrome.
- Frontend (from `examples/frontend/`): `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; `cargo clippy --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo test --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`; `trunk serve --release true` to run it. Extension: `npm ci --ignore-scripts && npm run package:frontend-extension` from the root.
- FFI: `cargo build -p rings-node --features ffi`; `RINGS_FFI_REQUIRE_LIBRARY=1 pytest examples/ffi/tests`.
- Docs: `mdbook build docs`; `mdbook serve docs` to preview.
- Decode-boundary smoke: set `RINGS_DECODE_BOUNDARY_SEED` and `RINGS_DECODE_BOUNDARY_CASES`, then run the `decode_boundary` test filters for `rings-core`, `rings-transport`, and `rings-node`.
- Gates a change must pass (`.github/workflows/qaci.yml`): clippy with `-D warnings` on the native, wasm, and ffi feature sets; `cargo +nightly fmt --check`; rustdoc with `-D warnings`; `taplo format --check`; typos; cargo-deny; Miri on core invariants; the native, wasm, frontend, dweb, gateway, and generated decode-boundary test suites; the docs build.

## Conventions

- Layering: `core` is protocol only; application registries and descriptors live in `node`; `rpc` protos are plain DTO mirrors. Check every new type's vocabulary against the crate it lands in.
- Pure core, imperative shell: keep state transitions pure and explicit, represent effects as data, and confine IO to the interpreter that runs them.
- Lints are declared in the workspace `[lints]`: `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `panic`, `todo`, `unimplemented`, and `indexing_slicing` are denied on production paths. Fix the underlying structure (a struct for many arguments, `Box` for a large enum variant) rather than suppressing lints.
- Imports: one item per `use` line, no glob imports. Prefer method forms (`deref()`, `as_ref()`, `as_slice()`, `clone()`) to `&` and `*` in expressions.
- Tests are deterministic: wait for a concrete event (a generation counter, a channel message, a state predicate) and run topology tests on the `dummy` transport.
- Comments and docs explain why, not what. When a behaviour or boundary changes, update every comment and document that states it in the same commit.
- Commit messages, pull requests, and reviews are written in English. The workspace version in `Cargo.toml` is bumped with user-visible changes.
- License: AGPL-3.0-only for every crate, the frontend, and the npm package (`LICENSE`, the `license` fields, `deny.toml`). Derived works and network services built on Rings publish their source under the AGPL; a commercial license is available from Rings Network on request.

## Optional

- [crates.io: rings-node](https://crates.io/crates/rings-node), [docs.rs](https://docs.rs/rings-node), [npm: @ringsnetwork/rings-node](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ringsnetwork/rings-node).
- [Releases](https://github.com/RingsNetwork/rings/releases): prebuilt `rings` for macOS (x86_64, aarch64) and Linux (x86_64 musl, aarch64 gnu), and the wasm package; one-line installer at `install.sh` (https://rings.rs/install.sh) and static service templates under `contrib/`.
- Public seed node: https://node.rings.rs. Its external handshake (`nodeDid`, `answerOffer`, `acceptAnswer`) is public; status and control methods use its Bearer token.
- Official X (Twitter) account: https://x.com/RingsNetworkio.
